title: Rugged tablet for Fergus: UK buyer's guide
meta_description: Fergus Go needs Android 8.0 or later and now queues photos, notes and time entries offline. The Tuga A8 runs Android 12 with 4G and a 1000 nit screen.
intro: Fergus is job management software for trades. Its website describes quoting, scheduling and crew management, job tracking through a Job Card, invoicing, reporting and certificates, and says support is offered across Australia, New Zealand and the United Kingdom, with a UK version of the site. The field side runs in the Fergus Go app, which the vendor's site says works on Android and iOS.

For the person doing the work, the app is where scheduled jobs, time entries, job notes, photos, forms, certificates and signatures live. That means a device used in lofts, plant rooms, roof spaces and building sites, often in the rain or full sun, and carried in and out of a van all day, which is where a consumer tablet in a slim case tends to give up.

This page sets out what Fergus publishes about the devices and connections it needs, which Tuga rugged devices meet those published requirements, where a Windows tablet fits for the office side, and how a UK trade business can buy a single unit to try before buying for the whole team.

requirements.requirement: Platform: Android 8.0 or later, from Google Play
requirements.detail: The Google Play listing for Fergus Go (package com.fergus.app, developer Fergus Software Ltd., version 3.13.1, updated 1 October 2026 at the time of checking) has a minimum API level of 26, which is Android 8.0, and shows device chips for Phone and Tablet. The Fergus Go overview article links to that listing and lists no system requirements, so the Play listing is the published figure.

requirements.requirement: Memory, storage and screen size: not published
requirements.detail: Fergus publishes no RAM, storage, processor or screen-size requirement for mobile devices in the Google Play listing or the Fergus Go overview article we checked.

requirements.requirement: Offline: previously loaded data, time entries, photos and notes
requirements.detail: The vendor's 2026 release notes say Fergus Go 3.1.2 (February 2026) lets you access previously loaded data when offline. Version 3.12.0 (August 2026) took Offline Mode out of beta for all users, with timer and manual time entries, photos and job notes queued and synced when you reconnect, a banner showing offline status and a sync state on each record (Offline, Syncing or Synced). Data has to have been loaded while online before it can be viewed offline. We found no vendor figure for how much data is kept.

requirements.requirement: Photos and videos: device camera and album
requirements.detail: In Fergus Go you add photos and videos to a job from the Album or the Camera, and the vendor recommends setting captured photos to save to the camera roll under Settings, Camera Settings. Each item must not exceed 50MB, album or camera roll videos over 30 seconds give an error, and upload limits apply across web and the app. Only photos and videos can be uploaded in the app; other file types are uploaded on desktop. The article says Files and Photos work offline and upload automatically once you are back online.

requirements.requirement: Signatures: on certificates and sign-offs, captured on the screen
requirements.detail: For sign-off in Fergus Go, the signer taps the signature box and the signature is captured directly on the phone; once signed, a certificate cannot be edited unless the signature is removed. You can also record your own signature under Menu, Settings, Signature Capture, which the vendor says makes it available for completing certificates, a feature of the Certificates add-on. The articles we checked describe this on a phone, and do not state a screen size for signing. We found no article describing a customer signing a quote in the app.

requirements.requirement: Tap to Pay on Android: NFC and location on, no Android version published
requirements.detail: The vendor's Tap to Pay on Android article says Fergus Pay must be configured on your account, Location Services and NFC must be on, Tap to Pay must be switched on in the Fergus Go app, and the phone must support contactless payments. It publishes no minimum Android version and points to Stripe's list of supported devices. It does not say which countries Tap to Pay is available in, so confirm with Fergus before choosing a device for it.

requirements.requirement: Windows: no native app documented, no published hardware specification
requirements.detail: The vendor's site describes Fergus Go for Android and iOS and lists no Windows app. It names no supported browsers or minimum computer specification on the pages we checked, though its help articles refer to a desktop platform and web uploads.

recommended.why: Fergus Go's field work is jobs, time entries, notes, photos, forms and sign-off, not large drawings, so the 8 inch A8 gives a comfortable form and signature area in a tablet that still fits a van door pocket. It runs Android 12 with Google Play against the Play listing's minimum of Android 8.0. Fergus now queues time entries, photos and job notes offline, and the A8's dual SIM 4G helps them sync sooner on rural jobs and keeps the day's schedule current, since offline viewing only covers data already loaded. The 1000 nit screen stays readable outdoors, the removable 8000mAh battery lets a charged spare take over on a long day, and VESA mount points with pogo pin contacts let it dock in the van. It is sealed to IP67 and has no MIL-STD rating, so for the wettest or roughest work the A10 is the tougher choice. At £379 it costs £70 less than the A10.

It is sealed to IP68 and tested to MIL-STD-810H, neither of which the A8 has, so it suits teams who work in wet conditions, groundworks or anywhere a drop onto concrete is likely. Its 10.1 inch 1920 x 1200 screen shows more of a long form, a multi-line quote or a PDF plan at once. It runs Android 14 with Google Play, well above the Android 8.0 minimum, has 8GB of RAM and dual SIM 4G with built-in GPS. Against the A8, the screen is 350 nits rather than 1000, the battery is not listed as removable, and it costs £449, which is £70 more.

recommended.why: Fergus Go's Google Play listing carries a Phone device chip as well as Tablet, and the vendor's sign-off articles describe signing on a phone, so the 6 inch Tuga A6 is a fit for anyone who wants Fergus Go in a pocket or a belt holster at 277g. It runs Android 15 with Google Play, well above the Android 8.0 minimum, with 4G dual SIM, built-in GPS and a removable 5050mAh battery. Fergus publishes no RAM figure, so its 4GB of RAM cannot be checked against a vendor number; try it with your usual apps before buying for a team. The trade-off is screen area for forms and quotes. Its Zebra 2D scan engine is not a documented Fergus Go input. At £349 it is £30 less than the A8.

recommended.why: Fergus lists no Windows app, and the pages we checked name no supported browsers or computer specification, so the Tuga W10 is not a documented Fergus device. It runs Windows 11 Pro, so it can open the vendor's website in Edge or Chrome for office tasks such as the desktop-only file uploads the help centre mentions, but check your own Fergus account on it before buying. There is no vendor figure to check its Intel N100, 8GB RAM and 128GB storage against. It suits a site cabin, a workshop or a van used as an office, with Ethernet and HDMI for a fixed position. It is not the device for the field team: the offline queue described by the vendor belongs to the Fergus Go app, and the W10's 5MP rear camera is basic next to the 13MP cameras on the Android devices.

not_recommended_note: Fergus Go's offline mode covers previously loaded data, time entries, photos and job notes, and the vendor's notes say these sync when you reconnect, so fit a data SIM and load the day's jobs before you leave signal. Offline viewing is not described as covering jobs you have never opened, and we found no vendor figure for how much is stored. Tap to Pay on Android needs NFC, Location Services and Fergus Pay, which the A10, A8, A6 and W10 list NFC for, but Fergus publishes no minimum Android version for it and does not say where it is available, so do not buy a device for that feature without confirming with Fergus. We found no documented barcode, QR or NFC scanning in the Fergus Go articles we checked, so the A6's Zebra 2D scan engine and the W10's optional scanner and UHF RFID reader are not Fergus features. Fergus lists no Windows app, so the Tuga W10 should not be bought as a field device for it. Fergus does not name Tuga devices, and we do not describe any device as certified or tested by Fergus.
setup_steps: Create a Fergus account at fergus.com, or ask your account admin to add the technician as a user.
On the Tuga A8, A10 or A6, open Google Play and install Fergus Go (package com.fergus.app, developer Fergus Software Ltd.). Sign in with your Fergus details.
Accept the device prompts for the permissions your team uses, such as the camera for job photos and location if you use Tap to Pay.
In Fergus Go, open Menu, Settings, Camera Settings and check captured photos are set to save to the camera roll, as the vendor recommends.
Fit a data SIM. Offline work is queued and synced later, but loading new jobs needs a connection. Check the sync state shown on each record after working in a weak signal area.
Do the office work, such as quoting and uploading non-photo files, on the desktop version. On a Tuga W10, use Edge or Chrome and check it with your own account first.

For the A8 or A10, fit the vehicle mounting dock and a 12V car charger so the device charges between jobs; for the A6, add the belt holster. Fit a tempered glass screen protector before the device goes out on site.

faq.q: Will Fergus run on the Tuga A8?
faq.a: Fergus Go's Google Play listing sets a minimum of Android 8.0. The Tuga A8 runs Android 12 with Google Play, so it meets that figure, as do the A10 (Android 14) and the A6 (Android 15). Fergus publishes no RAM, storage or screen-size requirement. We do not describe any device as certified or tested by Fergus; these are the vendor's published figures set against the device specifications, so try the app on one unit before buying for a team.

faq.q: Does Fergus work offline on these devices?
faq.a: Partly, in the Fergus Go app. The vendor's release notes say previously loaded data can be viewed offline, and from version 3.12.0 time entries, photos and job notes are queued and synced when you reconnect. Jobs you have not loaded need a connection. The vendor does not describe the browser version as working offline.

faq.q: Can I take card payments by tapping a card on the tablet?
faq.a: Check with Fergus first. Its Tap to Pay on Android article needs NFC, Location Services and Fergus Pay, and the A8, A10 and A6 list NFC, but the vendor publishes no minimum Android version for it and does not say which countries it covers. Do not buy any device for that feature until Fergus confirms it for your account.

faq.q: Should I choose the A8 or the A10 for Fergus?
faq.a: The A8 suits most Fergus users: jobs, photos, forms and sign-off fit its 8 inch 1000 nit screen, the battery is removable, it docks in the van through its VESA mount points, and it costs £379. Choose the A10 at £449 if your team works in the wet or drops kit onto hard ground, because it is IP68 and MIL-STD-810H where the A8 is IP67 with no MIL-STD rating, or if you want the larger 10.1 inch 1920 x 1200 screen for long forms and plans.

faq.q: Can we trial one unit first, and do you invoice businesses?
faq.a: Yes to both. A single unit to try before buying for the team is welcome. Business buyers can request a quote and pay by bank transfer on a proforma invoice. Tuga Hardware is the trading name of Destello Tech Ltd and is not VAT registered, so there is no VAT to add to the £379 (A8), £449 (A10), £349 (A6) or £649 (W10) prices. Delivery is free within the UK in 7 to 10 working days, UK only, with 30-day returns and a 12-month warranty. Multi-unit discounts apply automatically: 3% at 2 units, 5% at 3 to 4, 8% at 5 to 9 and 10% at 10 or more.
